found: A correct selection was called wrong while the needle was still travelling to 15.
fix: Judge the gauge only once the needle has stopped (five readings over 5 s) and give the crew 5 s to move the lever.

found: In repeat runs a needle still creeping towards 15 was taken as settled: one false “ten set” in 9 runs.
fix: A trend test: the needle must not be moving. 9/9 since.

found: With live speech, clearance plus readback take ~12 s, so a correctly set MCP could be flagged before the crew had finished reading back.
fix: The grace period starts at the readback.

found: The first hand-height threshold flagged 3 of 6 normal images from three held-out image sets.
fix: Re-derived from the first set alone and tested on two sets made afterwards: 8/8 (24/24 over all six).

found: Two recordings captured another window in front of the simulator.
fix: Runs with an unreadable panel or a bright, non-cockpit frame are rejected, not scored.

found: Spark’s readings arrive 3.5–5 s after the frame is taken, so its callout came after speed was already 10 kt low: 0 of 4 runs in time.
fix: Call on the speed trend (where speed will be in 10 s, like the PFD’s trend arrow), with each reading timed at capture and applied the moment it arrives. Then in time in 6 of 6 fresh runs; over later runs 5 of 8. Spark is too slow for this alert about a third of the time; the on-device reader was in time in every run.

found: One misread altitude (918 ft while at 6,000) made Crosscheck think it was on final and raise the autothrottle alert.
fix: The phase comes from the median of the last three altitude readings.

found: A level-change descent (thrust at idle, the elevator holding speed) was read as “autothrottle not in speed”, twice.
fix: No alert while the pitch mode is holding speed.

found: The thrust-mode cell blanked for one frame during a mode change.
fix: The thrust and pitch modes must agree over consecutive readings.

found: On-device text recognition missed a plain “MCP SPD” on two frames in a row.
fix: Three readings in a row are required.

found: The readback “descend and maintain 4,000 LAS for 421” was dropped (“for” joined the callsign into 4421), and with no readback heard the MCP check fired 1 s before the crew set it.
fix: The callsign is also matched in the raw transcript; with no readback heard, the crew gets 15 s.

found: Spark’s readings arrive ~3.5 s after the frame; the crew set 11,000 at 26 s, Spark’s readings of it arrived from 33 s, and the 8 s grace had run out by the clock: a false “set niner thousand”.
fix: The grace is counted to the newest selector reading, not the clock, and Spark’s facts carry their capture time.

found: Voice Transcribe heard “climb and maintain one one thousand” as “climb and maintain 1000”, at 9,000 ft, in 3 runs in a row (and correctly in the others). In the first, Crosscheck flagged the correct readback against it; in the next two the guard below rejected it, leaving nothing to check: the bust and the readback error went uncalled. Once it heard a correct readback as \u201cmaintained 1000\u201d, adding a wrong readback callout to a caught bust.
fix: A climb to below the aircraft, or a descent to above it, is rejected as misheard and logged, and Crosscheck says “Confirm cleared altitude.” The two missed runs are counted as failures in the test matrix. The scorer now counts any unexpected callout as a wrong run. Since the last of these, a line whose value contradicts the aircraft is sent to Voice Transcribe a second time (“listen again”); it has not been needed in the runs since.

found: The misheard-number guard itself rejected a correct \u201cclimb and maintain 11000\u201d, because one altitude reading was misread as 68,193 ft at 9,000.
fix: The guard uses the median of the last three altitude readings, like the flight phase.

found: Spark was slow (readings 6–9 s after capture); four readings of the moving needle arrived together, looked settled at 5 when stamped on arrival, and Crosscheck said “five set” for 10.
fix: The flap facts carry their capture time, as the autothrottle’s do. Replayed that way, every recorded flaps run is right, this one included (“ten set”).

found: After the X-Plane demo’s 60 minutes the flight controls stop responding while the screen keeps drawing; two runs were invalid.
fix: The time-out dialog is recognised and X-Plane is restarted before the next run.

found: A laptop webcam sees only head and chest: neither measure told a slump from reading a checklist.
fix: The pilot watch needs a camera that sees the upper body and hands, as on a glareshield mount; it is tested on footage from that angle.
